population.span: in the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer among 25,871 men aged ≥50 and women aged ≥55, including 5,106 African Americans.

endpoint.span: Primary endpoints were major cardiovascular events (composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular mortality) and total invasive cancer.

estimate.span: During follow-up, there were 805 major cardiovascular events, including 386 in the n-3 and 419 in the placebo group (comparing omega-3 with placebo, HR=0.92; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-1.06; p=0.24)

ci.span: During follow-up, there were 805 major cardiovascular events, including 386 in the n-3 and 419 in the placebo group (comparing omega-3 with placebo, HR=0.92; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-1.06; p=0.24)

analysis_set.span: Treatment-effect analyses were based on the intention-to-treat principle, as described in the companion paper on vitamin D.

treatment_strategy.span: was a randomized, placebo-controlled, 2X2 factorial trial of vitamin D3 (2000IU/day) and marine omega-3 fatty acids (1 g/day)

follow_up.span: Study medication ceased as planned on December 31, 2017, yielding a median intervention period of 5.3 years (range 3.8-6.1 years).

entry_population_matches_question.why: The trial enrolled a usual-risk primary-prevention population, including adults with cardiovascular risk factors, without requiring elevated cardiovascular risk; the analysis matches ITT.
entry_population_matches_question.span: our trial, which tested n-3 fatty acids for primary prevention in a usual-risk population

notes: All field spans use held full text. The served HR and CI match the primary cardiovascular composite and full follow-up ITT analysis. The outcome metadata also names RR; the bound source estimate is HR and must retain that scale.
